title: A multilevel Analysis of Saudi Arabian Student 8th Grade Mathematics Achievement TIMSS 2011
extended_summary:
This paper examines which student- and school-level factors are associated with mathematics achievement among Saudi Arabian 8th-grade students in TIMSS 2011. The authors use hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) to account for the nested structure of students within schools and to estimate how much variation in mathematics performance exists within and between schools.

The study does not evaluate an intervention; instead, it analyzes existing TIMSS survey and achievement data. At the student level, the model includes home educational resources, liking mathematics, self-confidence in mathematics, engagement in mathematics learning, and value placed on learning mathematics. At the school level, it includes academic emphasis, school discipline and safety, and instruction affected by mathematics resource shortages.

The population is Saudi Arabian 8th-grade students and their schools. The results indicate that all five student-level variables significantly predict mathematics achievement, with self-confidence in mathematics showing the strongest positive association. At the school level, academic emphasis is positively associated with achievement, while instruction affected by mathematics resource shortages is negatively associated. School discipline and safety is not statistically significant in the final model. The paper concludes that both student attitudes/beliefs and school context matter for mathematics performance, and that about 35% of the variance lies between schools in the unconditional model.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational multilevel (HLM) analysis of TIMSS 2011 observational data, not an experiment. It has clear methodology and substantive modeling, but limited causal credibility and no random assignment.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported associations are informative but observational and context-specific to Saudi Arabian 8th-grade TIMSS data. The effects are statistically significant yet not directly evidence of an intervention impact on general or priority populations.

finding.finding_summary: This multilevel correlational study of Saudi Arabian TIMSS 2011 8th graders (n not reported in the excerpt) found that student and school factors significantly predicted mathematics achievement. Student confidence in mathematics was the strongest predictor (b=18.5 points per one-unit increase), while home educational resources, liking math, and valuing math were also positive predictors (b≈3.7-4.0), and student engagement was negative (b=-2.5 to -2.7). At the school level, emphasis on academic success was positive (b=7.9), resource shortages were negative (b=-4.0), and school discipline/safety was not significant (b=-1.4).
finding.measure: TIMSS 2011 8th-grade mathematics achievement plausible values / scale score

finding.finding_summary: The paper directly modeled several affective/student attitude variables as predictors of mathematics achievement rather than as outcomes. Self-confidence in mathematics had a strong positive association with achievement (b=18.5), while liking learning mathematics and valuing mathematics were positive but smaller (b≈3.7-4.0), and engagement in mathematics learning was negative (b=-2.5 to -2.7).
finding.measure: TIMSS student attitude scales: self-confidence, liking math, engagement, value of learning math

finding.finding_summary: At the school level, the model found that emphasis on academic success positively predicted mathematics achievement (b=7.9, p<.001), whereas instruction affected by mathematics resource shortages negatively predicted achievement (b=-4.0, p<.05). School discipline and safety was not statistically significant (b=-1.4).
finding.measure: School-level TIMSS indices: emphasis on academic success, discipline/safety, and mathematics resource shortages
